text: CHIEF: P1, JUMPS THE QUEUE ABOVE THE ESTIMAND REDEFINITIONS. Ruling at post-01M16322V0KXTSE97RB8V4J5TT. This is the only defect found tonight that corrupts the ALIGNMENT rather than a reported number, so every number computed downstream inherits it - fixing signature estimands while the alignment beneath them is biased is polishing the wrong layer. MECHANISM: hsmm.scala:727 mean(xs) = if xs.isEmpty then 1.0, used at :728 for RelationLayer.WorldTime and RelationLayer.Causal preservation priors. A recall with no explicit temporal and no causal relations gets prior 1.0 = perfectly preserved for both, which LOWERS THE COST of transitions preserving an order never observed. The aligner is therefore biased toward chronological, causally-ordered routes for exactly the recalls that supplied no such evidence - i.e. sparse, fragmented, disorganised accounts - and in the FLATTERING direction, making disorganised recall look more ordered. Same asymmetry as unresolved-as-external and unranked-as-external, but upstream of all of it. FIX SHAPE: absence of relations is not evidence of preservation. The prior must abstain or be explicitly uninformative rather than maximal; do not substitute 0.0 either, which asserts total violation - neither endpoint is the identity element for 'no evidence'. Per ADR 0003 the conditioning mass (count of observed relations in that layer) must travel with the prior, and a zero count means the layer contributes no preservation evidence to the cost at all. Mutation proof: set the empty case to 1.0 again and show a route-preference test goes red; a test that cannot distinguish 'no relations' from 'all relations preserved' is not load-bearing.
